description:
FILED s481b (2026-09-10, Opus) while measuring the critical-infrastructure
milestone (#1607).  Found as the top cause of the JSON-PP dist's board result.

WHERE.  cl/pcl-runtime.lisp, `perl-regex-to-ppcre` (near line 25870): CL-PPCRE
2.1.2 has no POSIX-class syntax, so PCL rewrites `[:NAME:]` into explicit
ranges with

    (cl-ppcre:regex-replace-all "\\[:(\\w+):\\]" pat (lambda (match class-name)
      (cond ((equal class-name "alpha") "a-zA-Z") ... (t match))))

TWO GAPS, both of them the rule-12 silent fall-through `(t match)`:

  (1) The matcher `\[:(\w+):\]` does NOT match the NEGATED spelling
      `[:^NAME:]` (perl spells the complement that way inside a bracket
      expression).  The text reaches CL-PPCRE unchanged, where `[[:^cntrl:]]`
      parses as a bracket class of the literal characters `[ : ^ c n t r l`
      closed by the first `]`, followed by a LITERAL `]`.  So the pattern is
      not an error and does not match what it says.

  (2) The `cond` has no `ascii` arm.  perl has 14 POSIX classes; the table has
      13 (alpha alnum blank cntrl digit graph lower print punct space upper
      word xdigit) and `ascii` is the missing one.

REPRODUCER (scratch/s481b/probe-posix-negclass.pl + probe-posix-ascii.pl),
perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl on the same file:

    my $s = "A\x00 \x{100}Z";
    my $n = () = ($s =~ /([[:ascii:]])/g);    # perl 4   PCL 0
    my $n = () = ($s =~ /([[:^digit:]])/g);   # perl 5   PCL 0

    my $t = "A\x00B\tC\x1fD\x7fE";
    $t =~ s/([^\n\t\c?[:^cntrl:][:^ascii:]])/sprintf("<%02x>",ord $1)/eg;
    # perl  A<00>B\tC<1f>D\x7fE      PCL  unchanged (no match at all)

A THIRD, SEPARATE divergence in the same table, NOT part of this task: the
positive arms are ASCII-only approximations, so `[[:word:]]` matches 2 of the
3 characters perl matches in the string above (it misses `\x{100}`).  That is
the known Unicode approximation, not a fall-through.

WHY IT MATTERS -- this is not a corner.  JSON::PP escapes control characters
with exactly the negated spelling (JSON-PP-4.18-0/lib/JSON/PP.pm:546):

    $arg =~ s/([^\n\t\c?[:^cntrl:][:^ascii:]])/'\\u00' . unpack('H2', $1)/eg;

so under PCL that substitution never fires and the encoder emits the RAW
control byte where JSON requires `\u00XX`:

    JSON::PP->new->utf8->encode(["\x00\x01"])
        perl  16 bytes  5b225c75303030305c7530303031225d   ["�"]
        PCL    6 bytes  5b220001225d                       ["<00><01>"]

The output is invalid JSON, and PCL's own JSON::PP then dies decoding it
("invalid character 0x0 encountered while parsing JSON string").  Only
`->ascii` is correct, because `_encode_ascii` is a different branch.  This is
the top cause behind the 16 `t/099_binary*.t` files of the JSON-PP dist
(1536 planned rows each) and several of its PARTIAL files.

SHAPE OF THE FIX (not done here -- it is a `cl/` runtime change and this was a
measurement batch).  Add an `ascii` arm ("\\x{00}-\\x{7f}"), widen the matcher
to `\[:(\^?)(\w+):\]`, and give each class its COMPLEMENT range string for the
`^` spelling (they are all computable and stay inside a bracket expression, so
De Morgan through an enclosing `[^...]` is automatic): e.g. `[:^cntrl:]` ->
"\\x{20}-\\x{7e}\\x{80}-\\x{10ffff}", `[:^ascii:]` -> "\\x{80}-\\x{10ffff}".
Rule 12 says an unknown class NAME must then DIE naming it rather than
`(t match)`.  Bar: the guard belongs in a `Pl/t/regex-posix-01.t` with perl as
the oracle for all 14 classes in both spellings, plus a JSON::PP round-trip
row; a `cl/` change owes the full sweep and the re/ companion leg.
subject: SILENT WRONG: a NEGATED POSIX character class `[:^NAME:]` is not translated for CL-PPCRE at all, and `[:ascii:]` is missing from the positive table -- both fall through `(t match)` and the pattern then matches something else (usually nothing).  This is JSON::PP's control-character escape, so every JSON::PP encode of a control character emits INVALID JSON.
